Intercultural Theory|Iceberg Model.title: Iceberg Model of Culture
Intercultural Theory|Iceberg Model.subtitle: 文化冰山模型
Intercultural Theory|Iceberg Model.summary: Use the iceberg model to separate visible cultural products from deeper values, assumptions and worldview. It is a framing tool rather than a predictive law.
rules: Visible layer: food, dress, language, rituals, festivals and observable etiquette.
Hidden layer: values, beliefs, assumptions, attitudes to authority, concepts of self, time and relationships.
Misunderstandings often arise when people react to visible behavior without examining the hidden assumptions behind it.
traps: The model simplifies reality; culture is not literally split into only two layers.
Visible difference does not automatically mean deep value conflict.
Intercultural Theory|Iceberg Model.memory: Remember: what you notice first is only the tip; most meaning sits under the waterline.

Intercultural Theory|Bennett DMIS.title: Bennett’s DMIS
Intercultural Theory|Bennett DMIS.subtitle: 本尼特跨文化敏感性发展模式
Intercultural Theory|Bennett DMIS.summary: DMIS explains movement from ethnocentric to ethnorelative orientations in how people interpret cultural difference.
rules: Ethnocentric stages: Denial → Defense → Minimization.
Ethnorelative stages: Acceptance → Adaptation → Integration.
Progress means greater ability to interpret difference without reducing it to threat or sameness.
traps: The stages are developmental tendencies, not rigid labels for judging people.
Minimization can sound tolerant but may erase real difference.
Intercultural Theory|Bennett DMIS.memory: Think of a staircase from “They are wrong” to “Difference can be understood and integrated.”

Intercultural Theory|Berry Acculturation.title: Berry’s Acculturation Strategies
Intercultural Theory|Berry Acculturation.subtitle: 贝瑞文化适应策略
Intercultural Theory|Berry Acculturation.summary: Berry maps adaptation strategies with two questions: keep original culture? seek participation in the larger society?
rules: Integration: keep original culture + participate in larger society.
Assimilation: do not maintain original culture + participate in larger society.
Separation: maintain original culture + low participation in larger society.
Marginalization: low maintenance + low participation.
traps: These are relational strategies shaped by context, not simply personal preference.
Integration is not the same as total assimilation.
Intercultural Theory|Berry Acculturation.memory: Two yes/no questions create a four-box map.

Intercultural Theory|Cultural Intelligen.title: Cultural Intelligence (CQ)
Intercultural Theory|Cultural Intelligen.subtitle: 文化智商 / 文化智力
Intercultural Theory|Cultural Intelligen.summary: CQ explains how people function effectively across cultural contexts through knowledge, motivation and flexible action.
rules: Drive CQ: interest, confidence and motivation to function cross-culturally.
Knowledge CQ: understanding systems, norms and conventions.
Strategy CQ: planning, monitoring and revising one’s interpretation.
Action CQ: adapting verbal and nonverbal behavior appropriately.
traps: High CQ does not mean mimicking every behavior you see.
Knowledge without reflection and adjustment is not enough.
Intercultural Theory|Cultural Intelligen.memory: CQ works like four gears: want to learn, know the system, plan mindfully, act flexibly.

Intercultural Theory|Identity Negotiatio.title: Identity Negotiation Theory
Intercultural Theory|Identity Negotiatio.subtitle: 身份协商理论
Intercultural Theory|Identity Negotiatio.summary: Identity negotiation focuses on how people seek security, inclusion, trust and recognition while presenting themselves in intercultural interaction.
rules: Interaction quality improves when people feel understood, respected and affirmed.
Identity is not only carried by the self; it is negotiated through recognition from others.
Trust, empathy and mindful communication support smoother identity negotiation.
traps: Identity negotiation is broader than face-saving in a single conflict episode.
Recognition does not require full agreement.
Intercultural Theory|Identity Negotiatio.memory: Ask: Do I feel seen, safe and recognized here?

Intercultural Theory|CTI.title: Communication Theory of Identity (CTI)
Intercultural Theory|CTI.subtitle: 身份传播理论
Intercultural Theory|CTI.summary: CTI explains identity through layered frames and the gaps that can emerge among them.
rules: Personal frame: self-concept.
Enacted frame: identity communicated in interaction.
Relational frame: identity shaped in relationships.
Communal frame: identity grounded in group membership.
traps: A mismatch between frames is common and analytically important.
Do not reduce identity to nationality alone.
Intercultural Theory|CTI.memory: Think nested circles plus possible gaps between how I see myself and how identity is enacted or recognized.

Intercultural Theory|URT.title: Uncertainty Reduction Theory (URT)
Intercultural Theory|URT.subtitle: 不确定性降低理论
Intercultural Theory|URT.summary: URT examines how people seek information in initial interactions to make others more predictable and understandable.
rules: Passive strategy: observe.
Active strategy: seek information indirectly, for example through others or background research.
Interactive strategy: ask directly and engage.
traps: URT focuses on early interaction and prediction; AUM adds anxiety and mindful management.
More information is useful only if interpreted carefully.

Intercultural Theory|EVT.title: Expectancy Violations Theory (EVT)
Intercultural Theory|EVT.subtitle: 期待违背理论
Intercultural Theory|EVT.summary: EVT explains what happens when behavior departs from what we expected, especially in nonverbal and interactional contexts.
rules: People hold expectations about distance, tone, turn-taking and appropriateness.
A violation triggers interpretation: positive, negative or ambiguous.
The effect depends on context, relationship and perceived reward/credibility of the communicator.
traps: A violation is not automatically bad.
Do not confuse expectation violation with direct cultural disrespect before checking context.

Intercultural Theory|Attribution.title: Attribution Theory
Intercultural Theory|Attribution.subtitle: 归因理论
Intercultural Theory|Attribution.summary: Attribution theory explains how people interpret causes of behavior and why they may misread others across cultural contexts.
rules: Internal attribution: explain behavior by personality, intention or character.
External attribution: explain behavior by situation, role, rules or context.
Intercultural errors often arise when situational constraints are ignored.
traps: Fundamental attribution error overweights personal causes.
One unfamiliar behavior should not trigger sweeping character judgments.
Intercultural Theory|Attribution.memory: Before judging character, ask what the situation is doing.

Intercultural Theory|Co-cultural Theory.title: Co-cultural Theory
Intercultural Theory|Co-cultural Theory.subtitle: 共文化理论
Intercultural Theory|Co-cultural Theory.summary: Co-cultural theory studies how members of non-dominant groups communicate within structures shaped by dominant norms.
rules: Common preferred outcomes: assimilation, accommodation, separation.
Common communication orientations: nonassertive, assertive, aggressive.
Strategies are shaped by context, risk, power and desired visibility.
traps: Do not collapse all non-dominant groups into one experience.
Communication choice is shaped by power structure, not only personal style.

Intercultural Theory|Speech Codes.title: Speech Codes Theory
Intercultural Theory|Speech Codes.subtitle: 言语代码理论
Intercultural Theory|Speech Codes.summary: Speech codes theory reminds us that communities develop patterned ways of speaking, valuing and interpreting communication.
rules: Different communities develop different norms for directness, silence, emotion and authority.
Speech practices are tied to social meanings and identities.
To communicate well, identify the local code before evaluating the style.
traps: A community speech code is not identical to national culture.
One speaker may shift across multiple codes.
Intercultural Theory|Speech Codes.memory: Every group has a communication grammar beyond vocabulary.

Intercultural Theory|Cultural Humility.title: Cultural Humility
Intercultural Theory|Cultural Humility.subtitle: 文化谦逊
Intercultural Theory|Cultural Humility.summary: Cultural humility stresses lifelong self-reflection, openness and attention to power rather than assuming one can completely master another culture.
rules: Self-reflection is continuous.
Approach others with openness rather than expert certainty.
Notice power asymmetry and institutional effects, not only interpersonal style.
traps: Humility is not passivity or lack of standards.
Knowing facts about another culture is helpful but never complete.
Intercultural Theory|Cultural Humility.memory: From mastery posture to learning posture.

Intercultural Theory|Third Culture Build.title: Third Culture Building
Intercultural Theory|Third Culture Build.subtitle: 第三文化建构
Intercultural Theory|Third Culture Build.summary: Third culture building describes how interactants create a workable shared communication space rather than insisting that one side fully adopts the other side’s norms.
rules: Build a mutually acceptable local norm for the interaction.
Shared rules can concern timing, turn-taking, feedback or decision procedures.
The result is negotiated and practical, not culturally pure.
traps: Third culture is not simply splitting the difference mechanically.
A shared norm can still reflect unequal power if not examined.
Intercultural Theory|Third Culture Build.memory: Not my rules or your rules alone — build a workable “our rules.”

Intercultural Theory|Dialectical Approac.title: Dialectical Approach to Intercultural Communication
Intercultural Theory|Dialectical Approac.subtitle: 跨文化传播的辩证视角
Intercultural Theory|Dialectical Approac.summary: A dialectical approach highlights tensions that coexist rather than choosing one side as permanently correct.
rules: Common dialectics: cultural–individual, personal–contextual, differences–similarities, static–dynamic, history/past–present/future, privilege–disadvantage.
Effective analysis often requires holding both sides in view.
This approach is especially useful when binary stereotypes oversimplify reality.
traps: Dialectical thinking is not indecision; it is a way to handle complexity.
Similarity and difference often coexist.

Intercultural Theory|U-Curve Adaptation.title: U-Curve / W-Curve Adaptation
Intercultural Theory|U-Curve Adaptation.subtitle: U型 / W型适应曲线
Intercultural Theory|U-Curve Adaptation.summary: These adaptation curves describe emotional phases often discussed in study-abroad, migration or re-entry contexts.
rules: U-curve: honeymoon → crisis/culture shock → recovery → adjustment.
W-curve adds re-entry shock when returning home.
The model is best used as a heuristic pattern, not a universal timeline.
traps: Not everyone follows the same sequence or intensity.
Emotional cycles should not replace structural analysis of support and power.
Intercultural Theory|U-Curve Adaptation.memory: First excitement, then dip, then recovery; returning home can create a second dip.

Intercultural Theory|Trompenaars.title: Trompenaars & Hampden-Turner
Intercultural Theory|Trompenaars.subtitle: 特罗姆彭纳斯文化维度
Intercultural Theory|Trompenaars.summary: This framework compares how cultures handle rules, relationships, status, time and the environment, especially in organizational settings.
rules: Universalism vs Particularism.
Individualism vs Communitarianism.
Neutral vs Emotional; Specific vs Diffuse.
Achievement vs Ascription; Sequential vs Synchronic time; Internal vs External control.
traps: Do not mix Trompenaars dimensions with Hofstede labels without naming the framework.
The framework is most useful for organizational and managerial comparison.
Intercultural Theory|Trompenaars.memory: Ask how a culture handles rules, relationships, status, time and environment.

Intercultural Theory|Social Identity The.title: Social Identity Theory
Intercultural Theory|Social Identity The.subtitle: 社会身份理论
Intercultural Theory|Social Identity The.summary: Social identity theory explains how in-group and out-group categorization shapes perception, evaluation and behavior.
rules: People classify self and others into groups.
Identification with a group can affect solidarity and bias.
Comparison between groups can shape self-esteem and behavior.
traps: Group identification does not erase personal identity.
In-group preference is not identical to explicit hostility.
Intercultural Theory|Social Identity The.memory: Who counts as “we” often changes how “they” are seen.

Intercultural Theory|Intergroup Contact.title: Intergroup Contact Theory
Intercultural Theory|Intergroup Contact.subtitle: 群际接触理论
Intercultural Theory|Intergroup Contact.summary: Contact theory explains how contact can reduce prejudice when the interaction conditions are supportive.
rules: Classic facilitating conditions: equal status, common goals, cooperation and institutional support.
Meaningful contact can reduce anxiety and stereotype rigidity.
The quality of contact often matters more than simple frequency.
traps: Contact alone does not automatically reduce prejudice.
Unequal or competitive contact can reinforce hostility.
Intercultural Theory|Intergroup Contact.memory: Contact works best when people work with, not against, each other.

Intercultural Theory|Theory Map.title: Intercultural Theory Map
Intercultural Theory|Theory Map.subtitle: 跨文化理论总图
Intercultural Theory|Theory Map.summary: Use this atlas card as a navigation map: value frameworks, interaction theories, identity theories, adaptation theories and critical/power approaches answer different questions.
rules: Values: Hofstede, Trompenaars, Hall’s time/context emphasis.
Interaction: AUM, URT, EVT, CAT, face, conflict styles.
Identity: Identity Negotiation, CTI, Social Identity Theory.
Adaptation: Berry, U-curve, Cross-cultural Adaptation, CQ.
Critical / power: Co-cultural Theory, Cultural Humility, Dialectical Approach.
traps: No single theory explains every intercultural problem.
Choose the theory that matches the mechanism highlighted by the question stem.
Intercultural Theory|Theory Map.memory: First ask what kind of question this is, then choose the theory family.

Intercultural Theory|Hall.memory: Hall = hidden meaning + space + time. Ask where meaning is carried and how interaction is timed or distanced.

Intercultural Theory|Hofstede.memory: Think “country-level value dashboard,” not individual personality test.

Intercultural Theory|AUM.memory: AUM = fog + nerves. Uncertainty is cognitive fog; anxiety is emotional tension.

Intercultural Theory|Face Negotiation.memory: When dignity, embarrassment or reputation appears, face theory should come to mind.

Intercultural Theory|Conflict Management.memory: Map the style on two axes: concern for self and concern for others.

Intercultural Theory|CAT.memory: CAT = move closer, keep distance or hold steady in communication style.

Intercultural Theory|Identity.memory: Identity has layers and shifts by context; nationality is only one layer.

Intercultural Theory|Adaptation.memory: Stress can become learning when reflection and adjustment continue.

Intercultural Theory|Nonverbal Communica.memory: First identify the channel: space, touch, gesture, voice or time.

Intercultural Theory|Bias.memory: Belief → feeling → behavior: stereotype, prejudice, discrimination.

Intercultural Theory|Integrated Theory.memory: Diagnose the stem first: values, context, anxiety, face, strategy or adjustment?
